Consistent application for a sufficient duration is important because stopping too early can leave residual fungal spores that lead to reinfection, which is why at least about 10 days of use is often advised even if symptoms improve sooner [1]. Single-dose, film-forming topical options (e.g., Lamisil Once) can also be effective by creating a therapeutic film over the foot that delivers antifungal action after one application, which may help patients who have difficulty with daily applications, provided reinfection is avoided [1]. However, some research indicates that in more severe cases, topical creams may have limitations, including inadequate penetration to deeper infected layers and potential recurrence due to fungal resistance, so combining creams with preventive hygiene and, when needed, alternative or adjunctive approaches may be necessary [0]. In parallel with cream use, hygiene steps such as keeping feet dry, treating or replacing socks, and managing footwear to reduce fungal reservoirs help prevent reinfection and improve outcomes with topical therapy [1].
